children: The correctness test for the whole plugin system: turn every plugin off, and core still works — fully.

, Barkpark must still work. Not "boot but be useless" — work: the Phoenix API serves, Documents validate against their Schema, the bp CLI queries, and the Content Model is whole. This is the single test that proves the Plugin Behaviour highway is correct — any feature that breaks when its plugin is disabled was wrongly built into core, or core wrongly depended on the plugin.
Crucially, the invariant covers the Content Graph too. With all plugins off, core

, not plugin-mounted. A plugin like the Tasks plugin or Media plugin adds edges through its Edge Extractor, but the baseline reference-edge graph and its API exist without any plugin at all. So the Graph View and Graph Comparison fixtures render on a bare install.

This is what lets OnixEdit, Bulldocs, the Frt plugin, and the rest be genuinely optional. It also guards against the slow drift where a "plugin" quietly becomes load-bearing — the Indx engine, for instance, is optional precisely because Search degrades to Postgres Search when it's gone. The invariant earns its keep on every Production deploy: a clean install must serve before any plugin is switched on.
